asante-empire.name: Asante Empire
asante-empire.summary: An Akan state in what is now Ghana that lasted from 1701 to 1902, known for its military strength, wealth, and trade in gold and other goods.

kano-city.name: Kano
kano-city.summary: A city in northern Nigeria, a major hub of trans-Saharan trade for centuries and traditionally ruled by the Dabo dynasty of emirs since the 19th century.

sokoto-caliphate.name: Sokoto Caliphate
sokoto-caliphate.summary: A Sunni Muslim caliphate in West Africa founded by Usman dan Fodio in 1804, which at its height ruled 10–20 million people before falling to British conquest in 1903.

kanem-bornu-empire.name: Kanem-Bornu Empire
kanem-bornu-empire.summary: A long-lived empire around Lake Chad, founded around 700 CE and sustained by trans-Saharan trade, later re-centered from Kanem to the Bornu region after the 14th century.

heinrich-barth.name: Heinrich Barth
heinrich-barth.summary: German explorer of Africa (1821–1865), regarded as one of the greatest European explorers of the continent for his careful documentation of cultures and oral histories.

balanta-people.name: Balanta people
balanta-people.summary: An ethnic group of Guinea-Bissau, Guinea, Senegal, Cape Verde and the Gambia, the second-largest group in Guinea-Bissau; their name means 'those who resist' in Mandinka.

portuguese-guinea.name: Portuguese Guinea
portuguese-guinea.summary: A Portuguese colony in West Africa from 1588 until it gained independence as Guinea-Bissau in 1974.

senegambia.name: Senegambia
senegambia.summary: A West African region between the Senegal and Gambia rivers, spanning parts of modern Senegal, the Gambia, Guinea-Bissau and neighboring countries, historically a gateway to the empires of Ghana, Mali and Songhai.

groundnut-pyramids.name: Groundnut pyramids
groundnut-pyramids.summary: Pyramid-shaped stacks of peanut sacks built in Kano, Nigeria, that symbolized the region's wealth until oil replaced agriculture as the economic mainstay in the 1960s-70s.

batik.name: Batik
batik.summary: A wax-resist dyeing technique for patterning cloth, practiced since ancient times in places including Egypt, China and India, but most highly developed in Java, Indonesia.

great-mosque-of-djenn.name: Great Mosque of Djenné
great-mosque-of-djenn.summary: The largest adobe brick building in the world, in Djenné, Mali; first built around the 13th century, with the current structure dating from 1907.

benin-city.name: Benin City
benin-city.summary: Today the capital of Edo State in southern Nigeria and Nigeria's fourth-largest city, historically the seat of the Oba's palace.

oba-ruler.name: Oba
oba-ruler.summary: A pre-nominal royal title used by kings in Yorubaland and, by extension, the Kingdom of Benin, said to trace back to the legendary first oba, Oduduwa.

belanda-hitam.name: Belanda Hitam
belanda-hitam.summary: Indonesian term for "Black Dutchmen," West African soldiers, mostly Akan, recruited by the Dutch colonial army for service in the East Indies between 1831 and 1872.

dutch-gold-coast.name: Dutch Gold Coast
dutch-gold-coast.summary: Dutch-controlled stretch of West Africa's Gold Coast in modern Ghana, colonised from 1612 and ceded to Britain in 1872.

hausa-people.name: Hausa
hausa-people.summary: A West African ethnic group of around 86 million people, mainly in Niger and Nigeria, traditionally agricultural with an equestrian aristocratic tradition.

igbo-people.name: Igbo people
igbo-people.summary: An ethnic group native to present-day southeastern Nigeria, one of Africa's largest, who fought to establish an independent Biafra in the 1967–1970 Nigerian Civil War.

elmina.name: Elmina
elmina.summary: A coastal town in Ghana that became the first European settlement in West Africa after the Portuguese built a fort there in the 1470s, growing into a major trading center.

kansala.name: Kansala
kansala.summary: The last capital of Kaabu, a federation of Mandinka kingdoms in what is now Guinea-Bissau, destroyed in the 1867 Battle of Kansala.

kaabu.name: Kaabu
kaabu.summary: Federation of Mandinka kingdoms (1537-1867) in the Senegambia region, originally a military province of the Mali Empire; its capital Kansala fell to Fula forces in 1867.

alfa-molo.name: Alfa Molo Balde
alfa-molo.summary: Founder of Fuladu, a kingdom in the Casamance region of what is now Senegal.

anglo-ashanti-wars.name: Anglo-Ashanti wars
anglo-ashanti-wars.summary: A series of five conflicts between 1824 and 1900 between the Ashanti Empire and the British Empire, ending in the complete annexation of the Ashanti Empire by 1900.

west-africa-squadron.name: West Africa Squadron
west-africa-squadron.summary: A Royal Navy squadron formed in 1808 to suppress the Atlantic slave trade off West Africa, which captured about 6% of transatlantic slave ships and freed roughly 150,000 Africans.

slave-trade-act-1807.name: Slave Trade Act 1807
slave-trade-act-1807.summary: An 1807 British law prohibiting the Atlantic slave trade throughout the British Empire, though it did not free those already enslaved.

fouta-djallon.name: Futa Jallon
fouta-djallon.summary: A highland region in central Guinea, West Africa, that gave its name to a historic Fulani state governed from the capital Timbo.

osei-bonsu.name: Osei Bonsu
osei-bonsu.summary: Asantehene, or King of the Ashanti, who reigned into 1824, fighting the Fante confederation, dominating Gold Coast trade, and halting British expansion in the region.

samori-ture.name: Samori Ture
samori-ture.summary: Malinke Muslim cleric and military strategist (c. 1830–1900) who founded a West African empire and resisted French colonial rule from 1882 until his capture in 1898.

battle-of-kansala.name: Battle of Kansala
battle-of-kansala.summary: 1867 siege that destroyed the Kaabu federation's capital, fought by the Imamate of Futa Jallon allied with rebel Fula, ending Mandinka dominance over Africa's Atlantic coast.

fuladu.name: Fuladu
fuladu.summary: A historic Fula kingdom in the Upper Casamance region of southern Senegal, also reaching into the Gambia and Guinea-Bissau, and the last independent pre-colonial state in the area, lasting until 1903.

scramble-for-africa.name: Scramble for Africa
scramble-for-africa.summary: The invasion, conquest and colonisation of most of Africa by seven Western European powers in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, regulated by the 1884-85 Berlin Conference.

french-west-africa.name: French West Africa
french-west-africa.summary: A federation of eight French colonial territories in West Africa, eight times the size of mainland France, that existed from 1895 to 1958 with its capital at Dakar.

troupes-coloniales.name: Troupes coloniales
troupes-coloniales.summary: The colonial troops of the French colonial empire from 1900 to 1961, recruited from mainland France, settlers, and indigenous populations, who fought in the empire's conquest and both World Wars.

uss-cyane-1815.name: USS Cyane
uss-cyane-1815.summary: A Royal Navy sixth-rate warship captured by USS Constitution off Madeira in 1815 and renamed USS Cyane, later cruising off West Africa from 1820 to suppress the slave trade.

ajami-script.name: Ajami script
ajami-script.summary: An Arabic-derived script adapted to write African languages such as Hausa, Fula and Swahili, using extra dots or marks rather than new letters for sounds Arabic lacks.

omar-saidou-tall.name: Omar Saidou Tall
omar-saidou-tall.summary: Senegalese Tijani Sufi scholar and military commander (c. 1794–1864) who founded the short-lived Tukulor Empire across parts of West Africa.

s-gou.name: Ségou
s-gou.summary: A town in south-central Mali on the River Niger, about 235 km northeast of Bamako; it was capital of the Ségou Cercle and Ségou Region and Mali's fifth-largest town in 2009.

tijaniyyah.name: Tijaniyyah
tijaniyyah.summary: A Sufi order of Sunni Islam founded by Ahmad al-Tijani after a vision in 1781, originating in Algeria and spreading across the Maghreb and West Africa.

f-lix-dubois.name: Félix Dubois
f-lix-dubois.summary: A French journalist and explorer (1862–1945) who reported from newly occupied Timbuktu in 1894 and wrote a popular 1896 book about his travels in French West Africa.

kwame-nkrumah.name: Kwame Nkrumah
kwame-nkrumah.summary: Ghanaian politician (1909–1972) who led the Gold Coast to independence in 1957 as its first prime minister, then served as Ghana's first president until 1966, and championed Pan-Africanism.

gold-coast-british-colony.name: Gold Coast (British colony)
gold-coast-british-colony.summary: British Crown colony on West Africa's Gulf of Guinea coast, 1821 to 1957, named for the region's gold and later becoming independent Ghana.

obuasi.name: Obuasi
obuasi.summary: A gold-mining town in Ghana's Ashanti Region, home to one of the largest known gold deposits on Earth and the source of the historical name 'Gold Coast.'

ashanti-goldfields-corporation.name: Ashanti Goldfields Corporation
ashanti-goldfields-corporation.summary: A Ghanaian gold mining company founded in the 1890s whose Obuasi mine became one of the world's largest gold deposits; it merged with AngloGold in 2004.

galamsey.name: Galamsey
galamsey.summary: Illegal small-scale gold mining in Ghana, a term from the phrase 'gather them and sell,' which has caused extensive damage to the country's gold-rich forests.

ashanti-region.name: Ashanti Region
ashanti-region.summary: The most populous of Ghana's administrative regions, known for gold and cocoa production, with Kumasi as its capital.

anglogold-ashanti.name: AngloGold Ashanti
anglogold-ashanti.summary: A South African gold-mining company formed in 2004 by merging AngloGold with Ashanti Goldfields, now one of the world's largest gold miners.

berlin-conference.name: Berlin Conference
berlin-conference.summary: An 1884–85 meeting of colonial powers in Berlin that produced an agreement on European colonisation and trade in Africa, often linked to the Scramble for Africa.

kamerun.name: Kamerun
kamerun.summary: A Central African colony of the German Empire from 1884 to 1916, covering today's Cameroon plus parts of several neighboring countries.

gustav-nachtigal.name: Gustav Nachtigal
gustav-nachtigal.summary: A German military surgeon and explorer of Central and West Africa, and the German Empire's commissioner whose treaties led to Togoland and Kamerun becoming Germany's first colonies.

usman-dan-fodio.name: Usman dan Fodio
usman-dan-fodio.summary: A Fulani Islamic scholar (1754–1817) who led a religious revolution in West Africa, founded the Sokoto Caliphate in 1803, and wrote over a hundred books on religion and society.

sokoto-city.name: Sokoto (city)
sokoto-city.summary: A city in northwestern Nigeria near the Sokoto and Rima rivers, former capital of the Sokoto Caliphate and still an important centre of Islamic learning.

muhammed-bello.name: Muhammed Bello
muhammed-bello.summary: Second Caliph of Sokoto, reigning 1817 to 1837, son of founder Usman dan Fodio, who spread Islam and education and established Islamic courts.

togo-b-kingdom.name: Mlapa III
togo-b-kingdom.summary: Last ruling king of the Togo-Bè kingdom, who signed a treaty with German explorer Gustav Nachtigal on 5 July 1884, making the area a German protectorate.

togoville.name: Togoville
togoville.summary: A town in southern Togo on Lake Togo, originally known simply as Togo, after which both the lake and the country are named.

togoland.name: Togoland
togoland.summary: A German protectorate in West Africa from 1884 to 1914, covering present-day Togo and part of Ghana's Volta Region, later split into British and French zones.

blaise-diagne.name: Blaise Diagne
blaise-diagne.summary: A French Senegalese politician (1872–1934) who sat in France's Chamber of Deputies from 1914 to 1934, the first person of full West African descent elected to it.

four-communes.name: Four Communes
four-communes.summary: The four oldest French colonial towns in Senegal—Saint-Louis, Dakar, Gorée and Rufisque—whose residents gained French citizenship rights from 1848.

gor-e.name: Gorée
gor-e.summary: A small island off Dakar, Senegal, known as a site linked to the Atlantic slave trade and designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1978.

saint-louis-senegal.name: Saint-Louis
saint-louis-senegal.summary: City near the mouth of the Senegal River that served as capital of the French colony of Senegal from 1673 to 1902 and of French West Africa from 1895 to 1902.

rufisque.name: Rufisque
rufisque.summary: A city in Senegal's Dakar region, once an important port in its own right and now a suburb of Dakar, with a population of about 295,000.

awole-arogangan.name: Awole Arogangan
awole-arogangan.summary: Alaafin, or emperor, of the Oyo Empire in West Africa from 1789 to 1796, whose paranoid and vindictive reign set the stage for the empire's later collapse.

afonja.name: Afonja
afonja.summary: Supreme military commander (Are-Ona-Kakanfo) of the Oyo Empire, active from around the 1750s to 1813, and one of only four Yoruba baale to rule Ilorin, a city founded by his great-grandfather.

otto-von-bismarck.name: Otto von Bismarck
otto-von-bismarck.summary: German statesman (1815–1898) who oversaw the unification of Germany through three wars and served as its first chancellor from 1871 to 1890, known as the "Iron Chancellor."

louis-gustave-binger.name: Binger
louis-gustave-binger.summary: French officer and explorer (1856–1936) who traveled from Senegal to the Niger, disproved the existence of the supposed Mountains of Kong, and served as governor of Côte d'Ivoire from 1893 to 1898.

kong-empire.name: Kong Empire
kong-empire.summary: A pre-colonial West African trading state (1710-1898) centered on the city of Kong, built on merchant networks and Islamic scholarship until Samori Ture burned the city in 1898.

parfait-louis-monteil.name: Parfait-Louis Monteil
parfait-louis-monteil.summary: A French colonial military officer and explorer who, between 1890 and 1892, travelled from Senegal east to Lake Chad and then north across the Sahara to Tripoli.

africa-squadron.name: Africa Squadron
africa-squadron.summary: A US Navy unit that patrolled off West Africa from 1843 to 1861 to suppress the slave trade, coordinating loosely with, but operating separately from, Britain's own anti-slavery squadron.

webster-ashburton-treaty.name: Webster–Ashburton Treaty
webster-ashburton-treaty.summary: An 1842 treaty between the United States and Britain, signed under President John Tyler, that settled the Maine–New Brunswick border and other disputes left vague by the 1783 Treaty of Paris.

hugh-clapperton.name: Hugh Clapperton
hugh-clapperton.summary: British naval officer and explorer of West and Central Africa (1788–1827).

old-oyo.name: Old Oyo
old-oyo.summary: A now-abandoned city, also called Oyo-Ile, that was capital of the Oyo Empire and a major West African political and cultural center in what is now Nigeria, deserted since 1835.

ilorin.name: Ilorin
ilorin.summary: The capital city of Kwara State in Nigeria, considered a Yoruba city despite sitting in the North-Central region; its population was 777,667 in 2006.

jihad-of-usman-dan-fodio.name: Jihad of Usman dan Fodio
jihad-of-usman-dan-fodio.summary: A religious and military campaign begun in 1804 by scholar Usman dan Fodio against the Hausa kingdoms of what is now Nigeria, leading to the creation of the Sokoto Caliphate, one of 19th-century Africa's largest states.

ubuntu-philosophy.name: Ubuntu
ubuntu-philosophy.summary: A Bantu African value system emphasizing the interconnectedness of individuals with their society and world, often summarized as 'I am because we are.'

west-african-vod-n.name: Vodún
west-african-vod-n.summary: A West African traditional religion of the Aja, Ewe and Fon peoples teaching a supreme creator divinity ruling over lesser spirits called vodúns, with no central authority.

if-x.name: Ifá (Fá)
if-x.summary: A geomantic divination system originating among the Yoruba people of West Africa, overseen by the orisha Orunmila and practiced by initiates called babaláwo, which spread to other peoples and, through the slave trade, to the Americas.

nana-asma-u.name: Nana Asma'u
nana-asma-u.summary: Fula princess, poet, teacher and scholar (1793–1864), daughter of Sokoto Caliphate founder Usman dan Fodio, still revered in northern Nigeria.

adinkra-symbols.name: Adinkra symbols
adinkra-symbols.summary: Symbols of the Akan people of Ghana representing concepts and proverbs, used on fabrics, pottery, stools and architecture to convey traditional wisdom.

kingdom-of-gyaman.name: Kingdom of Gyaman
kingdom-of-gyaman.summary: A precolonial Akan kingdom spanning parts of modern Ghana and Ivory Coast, credited in oral tradition as the origin of the Adinkra symbols central to Akan culture.

kwame-anthony-appiah.name: Kwame Anthony Appiah
kwame-anthony-appiah.summary: A Ghanaian-English-American philosopher and writer on political philosophy, ethics and African intellectual history, and president of the American Academy of Arts and Letters since 2022.

b-hanzin.name: Béhanzin
b-hanzin.summary: King of Dahomey from 1890 to 1894 who led resistance to French colonization before his defeat in the Second Franco-Dahomean War and exile to Martinique.

dahomey.name: Kingdom of Dahomey
dahomey.summary: A West African kingdom in present-day Benin, existing from about 1600 to 1904, that grew powerful through conquest, the Atlantic slave trade, and an all-female military unit called the Dahomey Amazons.

chiwara.name: Chiwara
chiwara.summary: A ritual object shaped like an antelope, used by an initiation society among the Bambara of Mali to teach young men social and agricultural values.

soci-t-de-g-ographie.name: Société de Géographie
soci-t-de-g-ographie.summary: The world's oldest geographical society, founded in Paris in 1821, which has published a journal since 1822 and hosted major geographic lectures and decisions.

alexander-gordon-laing.name: Gordon Laing
alexander-gordon-laing.summary: A Scottish explorer (1794-1826), the first European to reach Timbuktu, arriving in August 1826 via a northern route; he was killed five weeks after leaving the city.

ren-cailli.name: René Caillié
ren-cailli.summary: A French explorer (1799–1838) and the first European known to travel to Timbuktu and return alive, having disguised himself as a Muslim to make the journey.

british-west-africa.name: British West Africa
british-west-africa.summary: Collective name for British colonial settlements in West Africa, which became the independent countries of the Gambia, Sierra Leone, Ghana and Nigeria.

egungun.name: Egungun
egungun.summary: Yoruba masquerade or masked figure for ancestor reverence, representing the spirits of the dead as they periodically revisit the living community.

haitian-vodou.name: Haitian Vodou
haitian-vodou.summary: An African diasporic religion that developed in Haiti between the 16th and 19th centuries, blending West and Central African traditions with Catholicism and centered on spirits called lwa.

louisiana-voodoo.name: Louisiana Voodoo
louisiana-voodoo.summary: African diasporic religion practiced in Louisiana and the Mississippi Valley from the 18th to early 20th century, blending West and Central African traditions with Haitian Vodou and Catholicism.

candombl-jeje.name: Candomblé Jejé
candombl-jeje.summary: One of the main branches of Candomblé, rooted in the beliefs of the Adja, Fon and Ewe peoples from what is now southeastern Ghana, Togo, Benin and southwestern Nigeria.

robert-adams-sailor.name: Robert Adams
robert-adams-sailor.summary: American sailor who claimed to have been enslaved in North Africa from 1810 to 1814 and to have visited Timbuktu; his 1816 published narrative is now widely considered a fabrication.
